questions.q: An 'adequate diet' (often called a balanced diet) is defined as a meal that contains:
options: Only large amounts of carbohydrates to give energy.
All the necessary food nutrients in their correct proportions for healthy growth and maintenance.
Food items imported strictly from foreign countries.
Mostly meats and artificial sugary drinks.
questions.explain: An adequate or balanced diet must include the six classes of food (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water) in the right amounts for optimal health.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What is the primary nutritional and economic benefit of 'eating food in season'?
options: It ensures the food is usually scarce and very expensive.
The foods are at their peak of freshness, highest nutritional value, and usually cheaper due to abundance.
It forces people to eat foods they are highly allergic to.
The food lacks essential vitamins because of over-ripening.
questions.explain: Fruits and vegetables consumed during their harvest season are abundant, making them cheaper, and they are fresher and more nutritious since they haven't been stored artificially for long periods.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design

questions.q: Which of the following is a fundamental healthy eating habit?
options: Eating directly from a dirty cooking pot.
Washing hands thoroughly with soap and water before and after eating.
Watching television loudly while forcing food down the throat.
Sleeping immediately with a mouthful of food.
questions.explain: Washing hands before meals prevents the transfer of harmful bacteria and dirt from the hands into the mouth, significantly reducing the risk of illness.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design

questions.q: Biologically, why is it highly recommended to 'chew food properly' before swallowing?
options: It increases the volume of the stomach permanently.
It turns the food into water immediately.
It breaks down food particles to prevent choking and mixes it with saliva to begin the digestion of carbohydrates.
It stops the teeth from growing too long.
questions.explain: Chewing physically breaks food down for safer swallowing, and the enzymes in saliva (like ptyalin) start the chemical digestion process right in the mouth.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What is the main danger associated with talking while having food in your mouth?
options: It causes rapid weight loss.
It offends the chef who cooked the food.
The food can accidentally enter the windpipe (trachea) and cause severe choking.
It makes the food taste bitter.
questions.explain: Talking while chewing can cause the epiglottis to remain open, allowing food particles to slip into the windpipe instead of the esophagus, leading to choking.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design

questions.q: A severe long-term effect of poor and unhealthy feeding practices, particularly a lack of sufficient nutrients, is termed:
options: Hydration
Malnutrition
Immunization
Puberty
questions.explain: Malnutrition occurs when the body does not get enough of the right nutrients, leading to conditions like kwashiorkor, rickets, or severe weight loss.

questions.q: Taking excessively large mouthfuls of food and swallowing rapidly can lead to which immediate discomfort?
options: Immediate height gain
Indigestion and heartburn
Improved night vision
Stronger leg muscles
questions.explain: Eating too quickly and swallowing large chunks of unchewed food places stress on the stomach, leading to trapped gas, indigestion, and discomfort.

Substances intentionally added to food to improve its taste, appearance, texture, or shelf-life.
The plastic wrapping used to package fast food.
Foods that naturally contain no calories.
questions.explain: Food additives include things like food colorings, artificial flavorings (like MSG), and preservatives added during processing to enhance the product.

questions.q: An example of a potential misuse of a food additive is:
options: Adding a pinch of salt to a large pot of soup for taste.
Using chemical dyes to make spoiled meat look fresh and red.
Adding natural lemon juice to preserve fruit slices.
Fortifying flour with Vitamin A.
questions.explain: Using additives to deceive the consumer by masking poor quality or spoiled food is a dangerous and unethical misuse of food additives.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design

questions.q: How does a 'food contaminant' differ from a 'food additive'?
options: Contaminants are always sweet, while additives are bitter.
Contaminants are sold in grocery stores, while additives are not.
A contaminant is a harmful substance unintentionally introduced into the food, while an additive is added on purpose.
Additives only come from animals, whereas contaminants are strictly plant-based.
questions.explain: Contaminants (like stones, rat droppings, or salmonella bacteria) enter food by accident through poor handling, while additives are deliberately included by manufacturers.

questions.q: Which of the following food items represents a food substance that must NEVER be consumed?
options: Yam tubers stored in a dark, dry barn.
Canned food that is heavily rusted, expired, and severely dented.
Fresh green leafy vegetables.
Well-cooked chicken meat.
questions.explain: Bulging, severely dented, rusted, or expired canned goods run a high risk of containing deadly bacteria, such as the ones causing botulism, and should be discarded.

questions.q: What is one of the most severe physiological effects of prolonged drug abuse on the human body?
options: Increased academic intelligence and creativity
Severe damage to internal organs like the liver and brain, leading to addiction.
Improved resistance against all types of common colds.
Faster healing of physical skin wounds.
questions.explain: Long-term drug abuse chemically alters the brain causing addiction, and severely damages vital filtering organs like the liver and the kidneys.

questions.q: Taking small quantities of food at a time during a meal is a healthy eating habit because it:
options: Forces other people to wait for you.
Makes the food grow colder faster.
Prevents choking and aids in thoroughly chewing and digesting the food.
Allows the eater to talk simultaneously with food in their mouth.
questions.explain: Taking small bites ensures that the food can be comfortably and adequately chewed, which minimizes the risk of choking and greatly improves digestion.

questions.q: Which of the following is a potential method for consumers to detect the misuse of food colorants (additives) in items like fresh raw meat or palm oil?
options: Listening to the food to hear if it makes a fizzing sound.
Observing if the color washes off easily or stains the hands unnaturally red or orange.
Checking if the food suddenly jumps when touched.
Microwaving the food until it turns to ash.
questions.explain: Fraudulent sellers sometimes add chemical dyes (like Sudan IV in palm oil) to make poor-quality food look vibrant. These artificial colorants often stain hands intensely or wash off differently than natural pigments.

questions.q: Food adulteration refers to the dangerous practice of:
options: Cooking food completely until it is safe to eat.
Deliberately adding inferior, harmful, or cheaper substances to food to increase quantity or fake its quality for profit.
Preserving food safely in a freezer for months.
Serving food to an adult.
questions.explain: Adulteration is the unethical addition of non-food or inferior items (like adding sand to grains or chalk to flour) to increase volume/weight and deceive consumers.
